drivingQuestion: Why does the court wait once the condemned woman has sat on the birthing stool?
outcomeNote: The mishna's distinction is grounded: the fetus that has begun to emerge is no longer part of the mother's body.

segments.he: יָשְׁבָה עַל הַמַּשְׁבֵּר וְכוּ׳. מַאי טַעְמָא? כֵּיוָן דְּעָקַר, גּוּפָא אַחֲרִינָא הוּא.
segments.en: § The mishna teaches: With regard to a woman taken to be executed who «sat on the travailing chair» in the throes of labor, the court waits to execute her until she gives birth. The Gemara asks: «What is the reason» for delaying the execution in this case? The Gemara answers: «Once» the fetus «uproots» from its place and begins to leave the woman’s body, «it is» considered «an independent body» and may not be killed together with the mother.
